Hint 1: Consider the biological significance of codons in DNA sequences. Each codon, a sequence of three nucleotides, corresponds to a specific amino acid or a stop signal during protein synthesis. This makes codons a fundamental unit of meaning in DNA sequences.

Hint 2: Think about the trade-off between compactness and preserving meaning. While a more compact representation might seem appealing, it should not come at the cost of losing important biological information encoded in the DNA sequence.
